raw_signal_observation: The config editor loads an existing configuration file into a text box and, on Save, deletes the config file when the resulting text is empty; non-empty text overwrites the file. The dialog marks edits unsaved and disables cancellation by outside dismissal while edited, but saving an empty document has no second confirmation.
material_claim: The code proves that Save-on-empty means delete-file. It does not establish whether this is the intended semantic equivalence between an empty config and no config, or an accidental destructive interaction that should require confirmation.
neta_next_move: Confirm whether an empty mpv.conf is intentionally represented by absence of the file and whether Save is expected to normalize empty content by deletion. Only then decide whether confirmation or a separate delete affordance is warranted.
reversal_condition: If maintainers state that empty-file preservation is semantically required, permit the narrow write-empty-file change. If empty and absent are equivalent by design, retain deletion unless a separate FIELD or OWNER decision justifies extra friction.
baseline_decision: BUILD: avoid deleting the configuration file merely because the editor is empty; either write an empty file or ask for explicit confirmation before deletion to prevent accidental loss.

evidence: Post-freeze issue search found user reports involving empty mpv.conf configurations, including issue #1092, but no admissible maintainer evidence that resolves whether an empty config file and an absent config file are intentionally equivalent in the Android editor.
The user report establishes that empty configurations are a real usage state, not that the editor's delete-on-empty representation is a defect.
adjudication.decision_delta: UNRESOLVED_DELTA_SCORE_ONLY: the HOLDOUT case creates a restraint delta, but adjudication did not resolve product intent. It is scored only and is not used to teach, replicate, counterexample, or promote any insight before Wave 1 closes.
adjudication.lesson: HOLDOUT score-only. Representation equivalence between empty and absent cannot be inferred from destructiveness alone; no learning update is permitted from this case before wave close.
